description: Two-moment cross-check of the Borromean/Brunnian Δ_λ magnitude identification (0-fit, from committed witnesses). data.verdict: TWO-MOMENT CROSS-CHECK FAILS — the Borromean/Brunnian magnitude identification does NOT survive the second moment (scope-(a), 0-fit). SIGNS derived at both A (Milnor parity (−1)^{A−1}: μ₃>0, μ₄<0). But the SAME framing gives f₃=c₃/μ₃=0.6308 (0.63×, the near-miss) and f₄=c₄/μ₄=0.01269 (~79× short) — INCONSISTENT by 49.72×. The A-trend is BACKWARDS: the physical residual moments GROW (|μ₄/μ₃|=9.752) while the Brunnian clusters SHRINK (|c₄/c₃|=0.1961), because the 4-link is O(h⁶) vs the 3-link's O(h⁴) — intrinsic topological suppression (first Milnor at length A ⇒ O(h^{2(A−1)})), un-tunable without a fit. DECOMPOSITION: the 49.72× splits into the intrinsic h-order 1/h²=22.88× (the framework's OWN proved O(h^{2(A−1)}) prediction) × a residual coefficient-scaling gap 2.173× (order-normalized coeff growth ĉ₄/ĉ₃=4.488 vs the moment 9.752). STRUCTURAL: since h=0.2091<1, the clusters c_A~h^{2(A−1)} VANISH as A grows while the moments grow — so the identification c_A=μ_A can hold at most at ONE A and is structurally excluded as a magnitude closure for the sequence. CONCLUSION: this DOWNGRADES the μ₃ 0.63× 'near-miss' toward a coincidence. The SIGN leg (Milnor parity) stands; the MAGNITUDE identification does not. No fit; μ_A never inverted; nothing wired.
